expectation: HH3 is a histone H3 stain and should be nuclear. If it is total H3, it should fill nearly every nucleus and match DAPI. If it is phospho-H3, it should mark scattered mitotic nuclei, densest in proliferative crypt or basal epithelium, as bright condensed chromatin.
observed: A: yellow follows the tissue outline and texture, with glow along the edges. B and C: signal lies in stroma, cytoplasm and the luminal border, plus blobs of debris; the blue nuclei stay mostly unlit. D: bright yellow blobs sit beside the nuclei, not on them.
why: The signal avoids nuclei and follows tissue texture, edges and debris, so it shows neither the pan-nuclear nor the mitotic-nuclear pattern expected for HH3.
notes: HH3 should be nuclear, but the yellow lies between and around the DAPI nuclei, mostly in stroma, at the lumen and in bright debris blobs, and glows along the tissue edge. No nuclear population is visible, at any scale.
